recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not change core Attachment.size or restore a core largeValue extension for this issue; if FHIR-56953 reaches a final decision, handle the largeValue type or constraint in the FHIR Extension Pack workflow.
issue_request: FHIR-19958 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core datatypes. It reported that Attachment.size could not describe files larger than about 2GB when typed as unsignedInt, and its recorded resolution proposed a largeValue extension on integer with decimal value plus an integer-value constraint.
initial_application: The explicit FHIR-19958-tagged application appears in ec83d5b5057f1402bdeb77453f5d214806de6b8c, which added largeValue extension content and the floor(value) = value invariant to the core general extensions spreadsheet. Separately, the earlier R5 datatype framework commit cbdf7d1e55dc4bfa1dc30fc526edee0491e05782 changed Attachment.size itself from unsignedInt to integer64, which directly removed the 2GB limit in current core.
additional_context: FHIR-25208 added the signed long integer datatype for large numbers, and FHIR-26937 clarified that integer64 serializes as a JSON string. source/fhir.ini keeps datatypes and the general extensions spreadsheet in active build scope, but core extension definitions were later moved out of the R5 source. The largeValue StructureDefinition now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack, where later unresolved FHIR-56953 asks whether its decimal value should become integer64; that extension-pack question is external and not final.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/datatypes/attachment.xml defines Attachment.size as integer64, source/datatypes.html defines integer64 as a 64-bit signed integer, and source/json.html documents integer64 JSON serialization as a string. The current R5 published Attachment StructureDefinition also reports Attachment.size as integer64, so the seed defect is already resolved in core.

related_jiras.note: Published issue that added the signed long integer datatype, now named integer64, which provides the native R5 solution for large Attachment.size values.
Published follow-up clarifying that integer64 and other newer integer types serialize as JSON strings.
Unresolved FHIR Extension Pack tracker about changing largeValue from decimal to integer64; it confirms the remaining extension question is external and not final.
